**Isaac Denning** · 2025-04-27 20:59 UTC

Hi, I'm the team member who went through the runtime analysis. My methodology was that I added time logging to the top and bottom of those four functions I wanted to focus on and then sent a thousand direct messages. After this finished, I subtracted each child function's runtime from its parent and then averaged across all runs. This way, I could isolate the runtimes so the child functions wouldn't oversaturate the work taken by the function itself.

I don't know if that reasoning made any sense, but either way, I chose this method when communicating the runtimes to my teammates. I apologize if that added some confusion.

Another thing to note: I tested the time it took for my functions to fetch the system time and log it, and it was enough to alter those results. I considered making a more efficient system since, at the time, my logging was appending the system time to a file while running, which I knew was not fast. ## ✔ do_delete_messages assumes messages from same stream & ...

*2025-04-30 to 2025-06-20 · 28 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20do_delete_messages.20assumes.20messages.20from.20same.20stream.20.26.20.2E.2E.2E/with/2164042)*

**Aman (whilstsomebody)** · 2025-04-30 11:02 UTC

Hi folks, 

I wanted to discuss a potential issue with the `do_delete_messages`function in `message_delete.py` as indicated [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/33561#discussion_r2062981268) by @Sahil Batra 

```python
def do_delete_messages(
    realm: Realm, messages: Iterable[Message], *, acting_user: UserProfile | None
) -> None:
    # messages in delete_message event belong to the same topic
    # or is a single direct message, as any other behaviour is not possible with
    # the current callers to this method.
    messages = list(messages)
    message_ids = [message.id for message in messages]
    if not message_ids:
        return

    event: DeleteMessagesEvent = {
        "type": "delete_message",
        "message_ids": message_ids,
    }

    sample_message = messages[0]
    message_type = "stream"
    users_to_notify = set()
    if not sample_message.is_stream_message():
        message_type = "private"
    archiving_chunk_size = (
        retention.STREAM_MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE
        if message_type == "stream"
        else retention.MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE
    )

    if message_type == "stream":
        stream_id = sample_message.recipient.type_id
        event["stream_id"] = stream_id
        event["topic"] = sample_message.topic_name()
        stream = Stream.objects.get(id=stream_id)
        archiving_chunk_size = retention.STREAM_MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE

    # We exclude long-term idle users, since they by definition have no active clients.
    users_to_notify = event_recipient_ids_for_action_on_messages(
        messages,
        channel=stream if message_type == "stream" else None,
    )

    if acting_user is not None:
        # Always send event to the user who deleted the message.
        users_to_notify.add(acting_user.id)

    move_messages_to_archive(message_ids, realm=realm, chunk_size=archiving_chunk_size)
    if message_type == "stream":
        check_update_first_message_id(realm, stream, message_ids, users_to_notify)

    event["message_type"] = message_type
    send_event_on_commit(realm, event, users_to_notify)
```

Currently, the function **assumes all messages belong to the same topic and stream**, but the `classify_messages` function can group messages from different topics and streams. 

The `classify_messages` function has been implemented in PR **[#33561](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/33561): Add option for marking a user as spammer in the "Deactivate user" popover**, which divides the messages so that we can have the option to delete either "messages from public streams only" or "all messages" when a user is marked as a spammer. Refer to **#design>unarchive channel**.

```python
def classify_messages(
    user_profile: UserProfile, messages: Iterable[Message]
) -> tuple[list[Message], list[Message]]:
    message_ids = [message.id for message in messages]

    message_stream_flags = {
        message.id: (message.is_public_stream_message(), message.is_private_stream_message())
        for message in Message.objects.filter(id__in=message_ids).only(
            "id", "recipient__type", "recipient__type_id"
        )
    }

    private_stream_messages = []
    public_stream_messages = []

    for message in messages:
        is_public, is_private = message_stream_flags.get(message.id, (False, False))
        if is_public:
            public_stream_messages.append(message)
        elif is_private:
            private_stream_messages.append(message)
    return private_stream_messages, public_stream_messages
```
This creates a mismatch in the event data, where the `message_ids` field may not align with the` topic` and `stream_id` fields.

Should we update `do_delete_messages` to support multi-topic deletion? If yes, how should the event structure be modified to handle this?  

Or is there any other way to carry out the same deletion process?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-01 18:33 UTC

Probably the simplest approach is to just categorize the messages and call `do_delete_messages` once per topic. 

But it would probably be better to do a prep PR that refactors `do_delete_messages` to categorize the messages by recipient/topic, and then do that looping itself. One event per topic is necessary for API reasons.

```python
def do_delete_messages(
    realm: Realm, messages: Iterable[Message], *, acting_user: UserProfile | None
) -> None:
    private_messages_by_recipient: defaultdict[int, list[Message]] = defaultdict(list)
    stream_messages_by_stream_and_topic: defaultdict[int, defaultdict[str, list[Message]]] = (
        defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(list))
    )

    for message in messages:
        if message.is_stream_message():
            stream_id = message.recipient.type_id
            topic_name = message.topic_name()
            stream_messages_by_stream_and_topic[stream_id][topic_name].append(message)
        else:
            recipient_id = message.recipient.id
            private_messages_by_recipient[recipient_id].append(message)

    for recipient_id, grouped_messages in private_messages_by_recipient.items():
        message_ids = [message.id for message in grouped_messages]
        if not message_ids:
            continue

        private_event: DeleteMessagesEvent = {
            "type": "delete_message",
            "message_ids": message_ids,
            "message_type": "private",
        }

        # We exclude long-term idle users, since they by definition have no active clients.
        users_to_notify = event_recipient_ids_for_action_on_messages(grouped_messages)

        if acting_user is not None:
            # Always send event to the user who deleted the message.
            users_to_notify.add(acting_user.id)

        move_messages_to_archive(message_ids, realm=realm, chunk_size=retention.MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE)
        send_event_on_commit(realm, private_event, users_to_notify)

    for stream_id, topics in stream_messages_by_stream_and_topic.items():
        for topic_name, grouped_messages in topics.items():
            message_ids = [message.id for message in grouped_messages]
            if not message_ids:
                continue

            event: DeleteMessagesEvent = {
                "type": "delete_message",
                "message_ids": message_ids,
                "message_type": "stream",
                "stream_id": stream_id,
                "topic": topic_name,
            }

            stream = Stream.objects.get(id=stream_id)

            # We exclude long-term idle users, since they by definition have no active clients.
            users_to_notify = event_recipient_ids_for_action_on_messages(
                grouped_messages,
                channel=stream,
            )

            if acting_user is not None:
                # Always send event to the user who deleted the message.
                users_to_notify.add(acting_user.id)

            move_messages_to_archive(
                message_ids, realm=realm, chunk_size=retention.STREAM_MESSAGE_BATCH_SIZE
            )
            check_update_first_message_id(realm, stream, message_ids, users_to_notify)
            send_event_on_commit(realm, event, users_to_notify)
```

## force-deactivate a group

*2025-05-07 to 2025-07-11 · 16 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/force-deactivate.20a.20group/with/2168825)*

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-07 12:33 UTC

In #34398 we are finishing up support for syncing groups via SCIM. For quick context, SCIM is a protocol allowing a 3rd party user/group management system to immediately push updates to users/groups to Zulip. Thus allowing  central management of  users/groups and having any changes immediately, automatically synced to Zulip.

In order to implement the `DELETE` method we [need to add a way to deactivate a group](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/34398#discussion_r2045152560). The challenge being that our current code doesn't support deactivating groups which are inside of supergroups or are used in any permissions. ``access_user_group_for_deactivation`` checks for those conditions, and disallows deactivation if needed. The SCIM implementation requires us to be able to untangle the group from any supergroups and permissions and allow it to get deactivated without corrupting the data - rather than just throw an error, as ``access_user_group_for_deactivation`` currently does.

We discussed how to approach this with @Shubham Padia and arrived at the following proposal for forcing deactivation of a group:
1) Remove the group from any supergroups using ``remove_subgroups_from_user_group``
2) If the group is part of an anonymous group used for a permission, remove it from the anonymous group.
3) If a permission is set to the group, we need a replacement value to set for the permission. For that purpose, we add a new field `revert_group_name` to `GroupPermissionSetting`; every permission will define what this replacement group should be - `role:owners` in most cases probably.

The reason we need the new field for (3), is that `GroupPermissionSetting.default_group_name` is not adequate. By replacing the group for the permission with `default_group_name`, we might actually grant the permissions to **more** users - so that's a bad idea. A constant replacement value like `role:nobody` or `role:owners` also doesn't work, as neither of these values works for every permission. We need a good way of supporting  permissions which need a different replacement group. So just adding an explicit field to configure this per-permission seems most robust.

Thoughts on this proposal?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-08 18:46 UTC

Yeah, I think that's a reasonable balance. We should try to write a rule in the comments defining the `revert_group_name` field describing how one should decide which permissions should revert in what way. 

(I'd expect most should do fine with `nobody` -- it'll just be the ones that if set to nobody would orphan something where we'd want different behavior).

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-10 22:16 UTC

Hmm, there's an additional knot that needs resolving. I think even should be considered a bug in some cases.

When checking if a group `A` can be deactivated, `access_user_group_for_deactivation` explicitly does **not** check whether the group `A` is involved in permissions of **deactivated** channels or groups.
https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/2320a8917e00b921870fd166005ed096efa7552a/zerver/lib/user_groups.py#L233-L235
```
    for stream in Stream.objects.filter(realm_id=user_group.realm_id, deactivated=False).filter(
        stream_setting_query
    ):
    ... <makes sure user_group is not involved in any permissions for the stream>
   ....
    for group in NamedUserGroup.objects.filter(
        realm_id=user_group.realm_id, deactivated=False
    ).filter(group_setting_query):
   ..... <similar check for permissions of group>
```

I think this is certainly a bug for `Stream`. Consider the sequence:
1. Set a permission `p` of channel `S` to group `A`.
2. Deactivate the channel `S`.
3. Now group `A` can be deactivated - it's permitted, as outlined above.
4. We support reactivating channels using `manage.py unarchive_channel`. So let's do that.
5. Now channel `S` is reactivated, with a permission pointing to a deactivated group. That's corrupted state.

Until now, we didn't support reactivation of groups, so technically the analogical scenario for a `NamedUserGroup` isn't possible - but with addition of SCIM, reactivation of groups will become possible, so we'll need to settle this.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-10 22:24 UTC

Should we just remove the `deactivated=False` filters in ``access_user_group_for_deactivation``? Might also require migrations to resolve the existence of any deactivated groups which are involved in permissions of deactivated channels/groups.

And moving forward, when deactivating a channel or user group, we can scrub its permissions to the newly discussed ``revert_group_name`` value - to ensure that such a deactivated object doesn't later prevent deactivation of a group due to having a permission pointing to it.

**Sahil Batra** · 2025-05-11 06:21 UTC

We discussed about this before in #**design>Support user group deactivation@2033111** .

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-11 10:18 UTC

Ahh, that's helpful. Sounds like that discussion stalled on

> We definitely cannot reset to defaults

so now that we figured we want to do the ``revert_group_name`` thing, it might make sense to proceed with using that for this problem too?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-11 23:02 UTC

@Shubham Padia @Sahil Batra Could you give it a look? I'd appreciate a general review of the approach + the `replacement_group_name` values chosen for all the `GroupPermissionSetting`s.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-12 18:44 UTC

Yeah, i don't have a strong stance on OWNER vs NOBODY. I think they're ultimately kind of "the same" in essence, because any permission set to NOBODY can still be modified by an `Owner` to any desired new value, correct? So fundamentally, Owners have all such permissions, even if they're technically set to `NOBODY`?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-13 22:42 UTC

Permissions still work on archived channels (say, the access to read the archived messages), so I think the bug might be that we should not permit any permissions on channel objects (deactivated or not) when deactivating a group. 

Permissions on a group are more messy, because, for example, you might want the group to have permissions on itself, and it's annoying if deactivating the group blows that up.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-05-13 22:43 UTC

I think NOBODY is more correct than OWNER most of the time -- having an empty input just feels like a more normal state than an "owners only" value. I think we only want to use `OWNERS` for cases where the group is not allowed to be empty.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-05-16 22:06 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> we should not permit any permissions on channel objects (deactivated or not) when deactivating a group.

The challenge is that with this approach, if you deactivate a channel with a permission pointing to group `G`, group `G` will be in a stuck state - you can't deactivate it, because of the channel. You can't fix it, because the channel is deactivated and you can't edit its permissions.

But I'm not sure in what sense "Permissions still work on archived channels"? Yes, reading permissions work, but that's via the public/private-shared-history/private-private-history channel  type - not via `GroupPermissionSetting`. So I think we could resolve it, in a lossy way, by just resetting every group permission on the channel to `replacement_group_name` (+ a migration to do backfix for existing deactivated channels).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-09 19:49 UTC

I think that `replacement_group_name` strategy works. I'm not convinced we need a backfill migration, given force-deactivation of groups doesn't exist yet?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-07-11 15:04 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> I think that `replacement_group_name` strategy works. I'm not convinced we need a backfill migration, given force-deactivation of groups doesn't exist yet?

It doesn't for groups, but it does for channels. So channels might already exist in a bugged state, due to what i described in #**backend>force-deactivate a group@2171642** 

If a channel with a group permission was deactivated => then the target group was  deactivated => the channel will be in a broken state the moment it gets reactivated. So we would want a migration to find any channel (active or deactivated) with a permission pointed to a deactivated group - and replace that with ``replacement_group_name`` group.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-11 23:11 UTC

I see. Yeah, that makes sense.

```ts
export function get_topic_link_content(
    stream_name: string,
    topic_name?: string,
    message_id?: string,
): {text: string; url: string} {
    const stream = stream_data.get_sub(stream_name);
    const stream_id = stream?.stream_id;
    assert(stream_id !== undefined);
    const escape = html_escape_markdown_syntax_characters;
    if (topic_name !== undefined) {
        const stream_topic_url = hash_util.by_stream_topic_url(stream_id, topic_name);
        if (message_id !== undefined) {
            return {
                text: `#${escape(stream_name)} > ${escape(topic_name)} @ 💬`,
                url: `${stream_topic_url}/near/${message_id}`,
            };
        }
        return {
            text: `#${escape(stream_name)} > ${escape(topic_name)}`,
            url: stream_topic_url,
        };
    }
    return {
        text: `#${escape(stream_name)}`,
        url: hash_util.channel_url_by_user_setting(stream_id),
    };
}

```

**Evy** · 2025-06-29 00:54 UTC

I'm gonna go with this for now:

```py
    cursor.execute(
        query,
        {
            # SQL doesn't allow "IN" with empty lists, so add an invalid ID to the start to
            # ensure the lists are never empty.
            "full_fetch_recipient_ids": (-1, *full_fetch_recipient_ids),
            "partial_fetch_recipient_ids": (-1, *partial_fetch_recipient_ids),
        },
    )
```

~~~ py
    @asynccontextmanager

            )
            print("WAITING FOR EVENTS")
            async with session.get(url, auth=self.auth, params=data) as response:
                assert response.status == 200
                yield (await response.json())["events"]

**EricGT** · 2025-05-29 12:02 UTC

With regards to my use cases

1.  **Initial replication**
    As noted in my earlier [question]([#development help > ✔ Specifics desired to avoid rate limit using Python API @ 💬](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/49-development-help/topic/.E2.9C.94.20Specifics.20desired.20to.20avoid.20rate.20limit.20using.20Python.20API/near/2181993)) .
   A proof of concept that I am still testing but is working as expected at present, and I am sure many know this but here is how it goes. Instead of using ([get_stream_topics](https://zulip.com/api/get-stream-topics)) to get a list of topic names then using [get_messages](https://zulip.com/api/get-messages) with a [narrow](https://zulip.com/api/get-messages#parameter-narrow) using the topic name, instead **do not** use the topic name in the narrow and only use anchor with a large `num_after`, which can be up to 5000. This is like using a [cursor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cursor_(databases)) with an SQL database, except in this case one has to manage the anchor value, first request with `oldest` then for each subsequent batch using the last message id in the previous batch, adding 1 then using that as the next anchor value.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-05-29 12:41 UTC

The "cursor" concept that you are using is definitely standard practice in the Zulip ecosystem, and the main app uses similar tactics for back-filling messages after page load. It's not completely clear to me why you chose to go from oldest to newest, instead of from newest to oldest, but I suspect it's fairly arbitrary for your use case, and I guess it's slightly easier and/or more efficient to build up the final data structures when moving in that direction.

For my own use case, I still want to avoid going back **too** far in the stream to get messages.  I really want to limit my messages to the set of messages for which one of their siblings is current.  This means, for example, that I might have some really ancient messages for long-running topics (because I want the user to see the whole conversation) while skipping over fairly recent messages in the stream (because they're part of a conversation that has just fallen outside the window of me caring about it any more).

## Allow others to edit a message

*2025-05-31 to 2026-09-09 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Allow.20others.20to.20edit.20a.20message/with/2184401)*

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2025-05-31 09:11 UTC

I'm working on #33051 in PR #34775 and an MVP is ready.

I've added a field `is_editable_by_others` in `AbstractMessage`. 
Before proceeding further, I wanted to confirm if this is the correct way, or we should take a different approach.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-04 22:57 UTC

Hmm. There's an argument it should be a group that's been given permission to edit it.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-04 22:57 UTC

I worry that doing so would prove unduly expensive in some way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-04 22:58 UTC

We should think about this really carefully, because adding new fields to that table is expensive.

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2025-06-07 04:48 UTC

Would using another table to track editable messages be better?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 00:26 UTC

So let's talk a bit about the data model tradeoffs:
- If we do a group-valued nullable column, that increases the size of the `Message` table slightly -- though the migration should be easy, since presumably this would be `nullable`. I expect we'd end up having code to hydrate `Message` objects being designed to bulk-fetch the groups as needed where not `None`, so that we only pay a performance cost if the message actually has been configured as editable. (I imagine we'd aim to avoid having the initial queries to bulk-fetch messages do the JOINs, since most of the time there will be 0 such messages).
- If we store editability metadata in a separate table, then we need to JOIN with that table whenever we're fetching messages, just like we join with `Reaction`. Probably not actually complicated, but if we were to add a handful of other fancy features, having each be its own table might start pushing us towards too many JOINs in queries to fetch messages.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 00:26 UTC

I think that first option seems probably cleaner.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 00:31 UTC

So to me that suggests a `can_edit_content_group` field on `AbstractMessage`. I guess here I'm proposing that it'd differ from most group-valued settings in that we'd store `None` rather than the `role:nobody` group for the case that the user has not "shared" the message for editing, just to keep null comparisons simpler without doing a JOIN.

The one annoying thing with it being group-valued is we'd need to manage deactivating a group that's been given access -- and I think our current model is that deactivated groups can't be the value of a permission elsewhere. So presumably the group deactivation code would need to be updated to find any messages referencing it using the ForeignKey index.

@Sahil Batra @Shubham Padia thoughts -- does that seem like a good data model for this? The feature as a whole is not of great importance, so I do want to be careful to not create problems more than make the feature itself easy to do.

**Shubham Padia** · 2025-06-09 05:21 UTC

I am wondering what was the nature of the requests made when people wanted their messages to be editable? Did they want their messages to be editable by a random set of users, system user groups or just a specific set of groups, e.g. moderators or administrators. 

If we start with a specific set of users, e.g. an item in the three dot-menu saying make this message editable by this channel's admins or make this message editable by realm admins, we can start the issue with a lower scope without worrying about implications of using a group there. If we see this feature being used a lot and we receive more than a few requests to wanting to assign a group for this feature, we can then migrate the setting to groups.

**Shubham Padia** · 2025-06-09 05:22 UTC

I am worried if this feature is not of great importance, we might be inserting a not so important feature in a critical path such as messages and we might face issues during the maintenance of that code path.

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2025-06-09 15:23 UTC

(replying to Shubham Padia)
> Did they want their messages to be editable by a random set of users, system user groups or just a specific set of groups, e.g. moderators or administrator

The issue description says:
> Only users with permissions to send messages to the current channel/topic (or maybe to edit messages there? TBD) should be allowed to edit someone else's message.

Maybe this should now be concretely decided.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-09 16:12 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> So presumably the group deactivation code would need to be updated to find any messages referencing it using the ForeignKey index.

We should make sure that it's indexed, so that we can do this query in finite time.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 17:00 UTC

Every Foreign key comes with an index, so no action required to achieve that.

**Sahil Batra** · 2025-06-09 18:01 UTC

The data model for using a nullable `UserGroup` foreign key field seems good, but yeah handling group being deactivated is somewhat different since an admin might be deactivating a group while the group may be used by some `Message` object of other user. Not sure if user other than sender can change the `can_edit_content_group` value for a message.

Maybe we can allow deactivating the group and set the `can_edit_content_group` field to `None` as a special case only for this permission.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-09 18:46 UTC

Yeah I think that's the way to do it. Needs a bit more logic to handle anonymous groups, but should be doable.

Product-wise, it's fine if the message sender has the value go to None -- the sender can always change it back later.

**Kislay Udbhav Verma** · 2025-07-07 14:45 UTC

I'm not sure how to we can use this user group approach to allow all participants of a channel/topic to edit a message.

Do we instead wish to make it like `can_subscribe_group` etc in channel settings?

**Saoirse** · 2026-08-28 16:24 UTC

Don't know how far we've come on this, but I have a proposal based on Tim's initial options that does a bit if both solutions.

1. Add a bit/bool field (we can bikeshed the name) to the Message table that indicates whether it is editable only by the owner or if it's editable by others.
2. Implement option 2 as proposed - store metadata separate table.

This has a few benefits:
1. Very minimal increase of the message table size. A bit/bool field is tiny.
2. No joins needed! The flag will give us all the info we need if we're just viewing the message in the stream. When we want to edit it (clicking the edit button or sending an edit message API request), only then do we look up which groups are permitted. This can be a simple `where ` with a filter for the message id. If 0 groups are returned or if none of my groups are returned access is denied (this is assuming we've already checked that I'm not the message owner).

Thoughts on this solution?

**Saoirse** · 2026-08-28 16:31 UTC

I imagine the metadata table would have a unique id (pk), a fk to the message id, and separate nullable columns to disambiguate type (group id, user id, etc.), with one always being set.

Adding permission to a group or user means adding a row to the table, and removing permission means deleting the row

## misuse of on_delete=CASCADE

*2025-06-03 to 2026-05-19 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/misuse.20of.20on_delete.3DCASCADE/with/2186305)*

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-06-03 19:05 UTC

One of the causes of #34803 (#**production help>cannot access web/desktop app@2186217**) is that the foreign key `RealmEmoji.author` has [`on_delete=CASCADE`](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/ref/models/fields/#django.db.models.ForeignKey.on_delete), i.e. deleting a `UserProfile` triggers automatic deletion of any `RealmEmoji` for which they’re the `author`. I went through all uses of `on_delete=CASCADE` to check for other suspicious ones:

| foreign key | target |
| --- | --- |
| `AbstractMessage.sender` | `UserProfile` |
| `AbstractMessage.recipient` | `Recipient` |
| `AbstractMessage.sending_client` | `Client` |
| `AbstractSubMessage.sender` | `UserProfile` |
| `AbstractAttachment.owner` | `UserProfile` |
| `PreregistrationUser.referred_by` | `UserProfile` |
| `MultiuseInvite.referred_by` | `UserProfile` |
| `UserStatus.client` | `Client` |
| `RealmAuditLog.acting_user` | `UserProfile` |
| `RealmEmoji.author` | `UserProfile` |
| `ScheduledMessageNotificationEmail.mentioned_user_group` | `NamedUserGroup` |
| `ScheduledMessage.sending_client` | `Client` |
| `ChannelEmailAddress.creator` | `UserProfile` |
| `UserActivity.client` | `Client` |

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-06-03 19:09 UTC

It is possible that the correct resolution in some of these cases is that we should never delete objects from the target model; if so, we should change those keys to `on_delete=PROTECT` or `on_delete=RESTRICT`. In other cases we may want to make the foreign key nullable with `on_delete=SET_NULL`.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-03 19:10 UTC

We don't delete `Client` rows, so I think those should be `PROTECT`?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-03 19:11 UTC

I think we currently "handle" the Message / Attachment / Recipient ones by re-parenting them in `do_delete_user`.  But I bet we don't handle submessages.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-03 19:11 UTC

And all of the rest are problematic.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-06-03 19:28 UTC

The ones we manually re-parent should also be `PROTECT` or `RESTRICT`.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-04 16:38 UTC

I think we should just stop deleting user objects for that code path. I don't think that model is buying us anything but bugs like this. @Mateusz Mandera thoughts?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2025-06-05 19:40 UTC

yeah I think we want to just overwrite the necessary `UserProfile` fields and explicitly delete the objects that we want deleted - rather than relying on any CASCADE  behavior at all; as we've discussed a few times before and I think at this point it's clearly the superior option to the current approach.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-05 20:33 UTC

Yeah, let's plan to rework it that way.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-05 20:34 UTC

(We will still want to audit all the foreign keys afterwards.)

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-05-19 14:52 UTC

I was reminded of this in #**api design>Deleting users@2462108** . We merged #35477 which addresses data integrity issues caused by `do_delete_user` functions, but implementing @Anders Kaseorg's suggestion of changing `on_delete` behavior just in case still seems good to have.

## E2EE - asymmetric key-pair on bouncer

*2025-06-04 to 2025-06-06 · 21 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/E2EE.20-.20asymmetric.20key-pair.20on.20bouncer/with/2187015)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-06-04 19:36 UTC

As per the [draft ZAP](https://github.com/prakhar1144/zulip-architecture/blob/encrypt-push-notification/zaps/0002-encrypt-push-notifications.md):

> * The push bouncer maintains a `push_registration_encryption_keys` map containing asymmetric key pairs (`{public_key: private_key}`), each generated to support key rotation. When a new key pair is created, the public key (`bouncer_public_key`) is baked into a new client release.
> * To support older clients, the bouncer continues to accept the older public keys for a period of time, allowing clients to upgrade. Once a sufficient portion of clients have updated, the corresponding old keys are removed from the map.

Here's a proposal to implement this:
* A management command to handle the `creation` and `deletion` of these keys. 
* A JSON file to store this map. We'll have to store `creation_datetime` in addition to the key pair.
```json
{
  "public_key": "whatever",
  "private_key": "whatever-2",
  "creation_datetime": "datetime"
}
```
* We should cache a map `{public_key: private_key}` using the JSON, in memory on bouncer startup to avoid repeated disk I/O, and update this whenever a key is added / deleted (which won't be frequent).

I think we'll end up using a [Hybrid Cryptosystem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybrid_cryptosystem) as asymmetric key algorithms alone are not  recommended for encrypting large size of data.

```
encrypted by mobile client, decrypted by the bouncer.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-06-05 13:52 UTC

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:15 UTC

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-06-05 14:24 UTC

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:24 UTC

Actually, I don't think that we get to do HPKE.  We don't actually have an online connection with which to do key exchange -- we have a single message.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:27 UTC

Hybrid encryption works on *bidirectional streams*, and only ones where you expect the connection to be long-lived so that the overhead of establishing the shared encryption key is worth the overhead.  We don't have such a stream -- and even if we somehow did, our 
"connection" is only one message long, and I expect the overhead would far outweigh the performance benefits of sending the (tiny!) message itself encrypted with symmetric encryption.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:29 UTC

Do you think that token + timestamp + 4-byte string is going to be more than 256 bytes?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:36 UTC

We can certainly choose a value which balances entropy, and allowing us to fit within one block -- not that having two blocks is much of an imposition, since as you point out the majority of decryptions doing this will be message payloads, not client registrations.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:40 UTC

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-05 14:50 UTC

The client having to encrypt registrations, or decrypt push notifications, is unlikely to be at all a CPU burden.  The server having to *encrypt* every message to a different asymmetric key for every client may well be a limiting factor, but that process is straightforward to parallelize per client to make use of multicore machines.  Another mitigating factor here is that the [message contents are also truncated at 200 bytes](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/b6f111cc0c9c5958a0f8b3d35245f7b6581c027d/zerver/lib/push_notifications.py#L942-L949), so they're not infinitely-large.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-06-05 23:41 UTC

If you’re concerning yourself with details like using RSA to encrypt more than 256 bytes of data, then you’re thinking about encryption at the wrong level. We want to use a standard high-level primitive like NaCl’s `crypto_box`. We *never ever* want to interact directly with a low-level primitive like RSA; that’s full of dangerous traps for people who aren’t professional cryptographers. (And we don’t want something based on RSA at all—elliptic curves are much faster with much smaller keys for equivalent security.)

PostgreSQL does not guarantee that CTEs are executed in the order in which they are declared.

From https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/queries-with.html#QUERIES-WITH-MODIFYING:
> The sub-statements in `WITH` are executed concurrently with each other and with the main query. Therefore, when using data-modifying statements in `WITH`, the order in which the specified updates actually happen is unpredictable.

We absolutely require the ordering to be predictable, so these must be separate statements.

It's also very unclear to me what you're hoping to achieve by using CTEs here, since there's already multiple statements in your SQL, and you're not using the return values of the CTEs in the other queries.  What made you choose to put these into a CTE?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-26 14:31 UTC

The retry *may* be concurrent, and we need to handle that.

For instance, assume a client is talking to the server through a loadbalancer.  Client sends request to loadbalancer, loadbalancer forwards to Zulip, which starts work.  Client's network resets, and it drops its connection to the loadbalancer; but the loadbalancer is helpfully still holding the connection open to Zulip, which may still be handling the request (i.e. is mid-transaction).  Client retries its request, because it knows its connection got reset.  This leads to two concurrent requests on the server for the same message post.

Concurrency is all about race conditions.  It's not *likely* that we'll hit it.  But the purpose of building this system is to make it resilient to those very infrequent cases.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-26 14:32 UTC

(the same case is possible without the loadbalancer, since uwsgi doesn't terminate backend requests when nginx's connection drops, but the case is clearer when thinking about it with the loadbalancer as a buffer)

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-06-26 14:34 UTC

It wouldn't be a very effective "idempotency key" if it was only idempotent except in race conditions. :)

**Bedo Khaled** · 2025-06-26 14:54 UTC

Here is my resonale behind approach:
## Goal
1. First-time request:  `identifier=Null`, we insert a new message and update the idempotency table accordingly.
2. Duplicate request:  `identifier!=NULL`, Do NOT insert or Update, just return the `identifier`.
3. The query should always return results, indicating whether the message id is new or cached from previous request, we need the new id to further proceed normally or the cached id so we can include it in the response.
## Approach

We have 3 CTEs:

`work_cte`:  runs only once and the result is stored (materialized) so when identifier is initially, it will stay null throughout the query.

`insertion_cte`:  inserts new message **CONDITIONALLY** if work wasn't done before (`identifier!=NULL`), returning the new message ID  `RETURNING {pk_name} AS message_id`

`update_cte`: Set the identifier, **CONDITIONALLY** if work wasn't done before, to the new message id returned by `insertion_cte`.

## Why do we need 3 CTEs ?
The first two are obvious, since they are being referenced more than once and return values.
For the third one, we logically don't but postgres requires just one statment after the CTEs definition.

**Wrong syntax**
```sql
With cte_1 AS(
),
cte_2 As(
)
--update statment
--select statment
```

**Correct syntax**
```sql
With cte_1 AS(
),
cte_2 As(
)
--select statment
```

For the final 3 select statment:
```sql
SELECT * FROM insertion_cte   -- fetches the new msg id, but this might return nothing if work is already done 
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM insertion_cte)  -- explicitly return NULL when work is done 
UNION ALL
SELECT identifier AS cached_id FROM work_cte;   -- returns the cached msg id, we could be Null
```

Simply, Those 3 select statments make us able in python to have a consistant length of data, it's currently `[(id),(None)] ` or `[(None),(id)] `

To say more simply:
- The first request to arrive grabs the lock on that idempotency key value and will actually do the request.
- Other requests with that idempotency key arriving while that request is running get the Conflict error -- i.e. failure to grab the lock for the idempotency key. Probably few clients will see this in practice, but it is possible if you say let folks double-click the send button.
- Once that first request completes, it returns a 200 (or appropriate error!) as the response and stores the result.
- Any requests that arrive with that same idempotency key arriving after the request completes get the stored result.

Correct?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-11-07 20:34 UTC

I think the biggest reason that it ends up hard to write a test case for this is that test cases run *inside transactions*.  So the naïve approach would be to spawn different processes, and use IPC to coordinate them stepping through the key phases in the order we want to prove the properties we need.

Except those other processes cannot be inside the test's transaction, so they will never see the results of it.  We need them to have separate database connections so they can have their own parallel database transactions, but they can't do that and *also* be inside a shared test's transaction.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-11-08 04:25 UTC

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-12-03 15:01 UTC

I'm not sure I agree with the distinction about "good" and "bad" clients in the case where the server's validation of the same data changes.  The "bad" client you're describing is just one that replayed the request -- which can happen intentionally (which is why I believe you're using "bad," since they're manually constructing a new request and thus "should" have a new Idempotency-Key), or *unintentionally* because the browser replayed the request (i.e. the actual double-posting bug we've seen).  So calling this a "bad" client is misleading; it may well be a buggy client, or proxy, or something else.  We shouldn't ascribe a value judgement to it.

And also, for that reason, I don't feel like this is the wrong behaviour on the part of the server!  You make the request with the same idempotency-key, you get *the same answer*, no matter what has changed on the server.  That's being idempotent.  I don't see any other way we could implement it.

Now, the second case, of a second request with different parameters, it's much easier to ascribe a valence to -- there's a contract that a new request *should* have a new idempotency-key, and there isn't any obvious way someone can *accidentally* replay a request with different parameters but the same idempotency-key.  This is a client being out of spec, and so it seems fine to have mildly surprising behaviour -- namely, that we "trust" the idempotecy key over the parameters, and give back the result for that key.  It would be *better* to tell the client they're operating out of spec (by implementing the Stripe trick) but I think the current behaviour isn't necessarily actually "wrong."

## de-duplicate channel properties

*2025-06-29 to 2025-07-01 · 8 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/de-duplicate.20channel.20properties/with/2207664)*

**Kunal Sharma** · 2025-06-29 15:26 UTC

While working on per-channel settings recently, I noticed that adding a new setting involves updating multiple dictionaries and locations, which makes the structure somewhat complex and repetitive. I discussed this with @Sahil Batra, and he too agreed with it. The same issue also exists in the web app code (though not for the group settings). It might be worth exploring ways to deduplicate these redundant entries and simplify the overall design.

Some of the files I can think of right now where the majority of these changes are required: `lib/subscriptions`, `lib/types`, `lib/event_types`, `lib/streams`.

@Sahil Batra would you like to expand on this?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-30 16:16 UTC

I am generally excited to reduce busywork, but I do think some care is required -- it's more important to have good type-checking and effective testing than to save a couple lines of easy changes.

One reason I have been bugging folks to sort lists of field parameters (E.g., #35060) rather than just always dumping new parameters at the bottom of functions is that it really helps reduce merge conflicts -- every pair of new fields will merge-conflict if added at the bottom, but if there's 50 fields, it's fairly unlikely that two new ones will sit next to each other in a sorted order.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-06-30 16:18 UTC

Definitely some of the functions in `streams.py` could benefit from the loops we use in the views code over permissions settings.

**Sahil Batra** · 2025-06-30 17:43 UTC

I also thought about this a bit. Yes we can loop over `Stream.stream_permission_group_settings` in some places but other than that I am not sure we can do anything as we are using `TypedDict`. 

Other than this we have many TypedDicts like a type for default stream dict, subscribed stream dict, never subscribed stream dict, etc. Maybe we can do something there by extracting common values in a single TypedDict and not having to define same fields multiple times in multiple types/

**Steve Howell** · 2025-07-01 01:20 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> One reason I have been bugging folks to sort lists of field parameters (E.g., #35060) rather than just always dumping new parameters at the bottom of functions is that it really helps reduce merge conflicts -- every pair of new fields will merge-conflict if added at the bottom, but if there's 50 fie …

I'm pretty obsessive about sorting things alphabetically within code once you get up to something like 7 or more thingies, unless there is a compelling reason to order them otherwise.  I have never regretted it.  And it's not really that hard.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-07-01 01:25 UTC

In vim you can select a block and do `!sort`, for example.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-07-01 01:29 UTC

## Fix narrow URLs in exported messages.

*2025-06-30 to 2025-07-02 · 9 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Fix.20narrow.20URLs.20in.20exported.20messages.2E/with/2208096)*

**Pieter K** · 2025-06-30 13:21 UTC

I'm opening this thread to talk about the progress on issue `Import process breaks near-links in the imported messages` #31100. The project has spawned several prep PRs, so I'm using this thread to recap the progress so far, and talk about my reasoning for some changes. Let me know if any part doesn't make sense!

---

Here is [a comment](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/32272#discussion_r1881047213) from @Tim Abbott regarding the overall implementation plan:
`````spoiler comment

> I think it's particularly visible here, but we have the wrong data structures for here, and it results in the parsing being wrong in corner cases that no known code produces, but should be valid. I think what you want to be doing is parsing the URL into a list[NarrowParameter] structure, and then lo …

`````
So far:
- We merged #33116 to add `parse_narrow_url` and refactor a `NeverNegatedNarrowTerm`.

So next, we need the `Filter` class to clean and update the list of terms we got from `parse_narrow_url`. 

I have #33590 for this, the `Filter` class has:
- term canonicalization and validation functions
- `Filter.operands` and `Filter.update_terms`
- Additionally, I also add `Filter.sort_terms`, It sorts a list of `NarrowTerm` using the same sorting algorithm [`Filter.sorted_term_types`](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/blob/main/web/src/filter.ts#L642C5-L685C6) uses.

Once we have that, we need a good way to turn a `list[NarrowTerm]` into a narrow URL.

**Pieter K** · 2025-06-30 13:21 UTC

### Current state of the narrow URL modules.

For that, we have the `topic_link_utils.py` and `url_encoding.py` modules. But at their current state, I feel like both aren't really ideal for our needs here.
- The `url_encoding.py` module was initially used in the events code path, so they mostly accept the wide message dict format (`MessageDict.wide_dict`). Most methods have parameters like this:
  `near_message_url(realm: Realm, message: dict[str, Any])` 
- The `topic_link_utils.py` module outputs link syntaxes ("#channel > topic > message"), whereas what we need here are narrow URLs, that because we're replacing the links `href` attribute in the messages `rendered_content`. The encoding logics in this module are baked into other methods, so no utility method like `encode_stream` that we can reuse.

On top of that, both aren't standardized to use the same encoding algorithm to encode strings like channel name and topic name. I think a prep work that'd be worth it to do is to:
- Refactor out common logics used to encode operands. The `url_encoding.py` has `encode_stream`, we can refactor similar functions that encode user_ids (for pm recipients), topics, etc. 
- standardize the encoding function both modules use, e.g., make `url_encoding.py` use `encode_hash_component` and `topic_link_utils.py` use `encode_stream`.
- (And probably also rename any string using "stream" to "channel")

This way, all modules can use the same encoding logic (including for our use case here) and we don't have to force either module to also accommodate the specs that we require here -- or be forced to perform additional steps to use the existing functions in those modules (e.g., convert our narrow terms to `wide_dict` or something like that).

I have #35021 for the refactor on narrow URL modules, it:
- Refactors a `encode_user_ids` and a `encode_full_name_and_id` out of existing functions.
- Updates `encode_stream` to use `encode_hash_component`.
- Updates `topic_link_utils` to use `encode_stream`.

**Pieter K** · 2025-06-30 13:22 UTC

## Generate narrow URL out of narrow terms.

Finally, we can discuss how to go about turning a list of narrow terms to narrow URLs. I think there are only 2 key things that we need to keep in mind when building narrow URLs:
- The URL fragment has to start with `/#narrow`
- Each term has to be encoded correctly

Additionally, the order of terms should start from the more general ones (`channel`, `dm`)  to specific ones (`with`, `near`). But links with unordered operands work too.

So that means, if we know how to encode each operator correctly, we can generate a narrow link out of any combination of terms. The steps I had in mind goes roughly like this:

> A list of narrow terms from `parse_narrow_url` ```python {operator: "topic", operand: "profile pictures", negated: False} {operator: "channel", operand: "3", negated: False} ``` 1. sort the terms first using `Filter.sort_terms`. ↓ ```python {operator: "channel", operand: "3", negated: False} {operat …

With this algorithm, we don't have to know what type of narrow URL we're working with and so, don't have to worry which narrow URL function to call for each operation. e.g, whether to call methods like `near_stream_message_url` or `near_pm_message_url`, etc.

I have a draft for this in #35056, it's the last commit, it's stacked on top of the 2 previous PRs I mentioned above.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-07-06 22:51 UTC

My `_get_node` function fairly succinctly demonstrates the structure of Zulip HTML, and you can see further details in [message_parser.py](https://github.com/showell/zulip-flet/blob/main/api/message_parser.py):

~~~ spoiler _get_node
~~~~ py
def _get_node(elem: Element) -> BaseNode:
    elem_class = elem.get("class") or ""

    if elem.tag == "a":
        if not elem_class:
            restrict_attributes(elem, "href")
            href = elem.get("href")
            assert href is not None
            return AnchorNode(href=href, children=get_child_nodes(elem))

        if elem_class == "message-link":
            return get_message_link_node(elem)

        if elem_class in ["stream", "stream-topic"]:
            return get_stream_link_node(elem)

    if elem.tag == "br":
        restrict_attributes(elem)
        forbid_children(elem)
        return BreakNode()

    if elem.tag == "div":
        if elem_class == "codehilite":
            return get_code_block_node(elem)
        if elem_class == "spoiler-block":
            return get_spoiler_node(elem)
        if elem_class == "message_inline_image":
            return get_inline_image_node(elem)
        if elem_class == "message_inline_image message_inline_video":
            return get_inline_video_node(elem)

    if elem.tag == "hr":
        restrict_attributes(elem)
        forbid_children(elem)
        return HrNode()

    if elem.tag == "img":
        if elem_class == "emoji":
            return get_emoji_image_node(elem)

    if elem.tag == "ol":
        return get_ordered_list_node(elem)

    if elem.tag == "span":
        if elem_class.startswith("emoji "):
            return get_emoji_span_node(elem)
        if elem_class in ["katex", "katex-display"]:
            return get_raw_katex_node(elem)
        if elem_class == "user-group-mention":
            return get_user_group_mention_node(elem, silent=False)
        if elem_class == "user-group-mention silent":
            return get_user_group_mention_node(elem, silent=True)
        if elem_class == "user-mention":
            return get_user_mention_node(elem, silent=False)
        if elem_class == "user-mention silent":
            return get_user_mention_node(elem, silent=True)

    if elem.tag == "table":
        return get_table_node(elem)

    if elem.tag == "time":
        return get_time_widget_node(elem)

    simple_nodes: dict[str, type[ContainerNode]] = dict(
        body=BodyNode,
        blockquote=BlockQuoteNode,
        code=CodeNode,
        em=EmNode,
        h1=Header1Node,
        h2=Header2Node,
        h3=Header3Node,
        h4=Header4Node,
        h5=Header5Node,
        h6=Header6Node,
        li=ListItemNode,
        p=ParagraphNode,
        strong=StrongNode,
        ul=UnorderedListNode,
    )

    # del is a keyword in Python
    simple_nodes["del"] = DelNode

    if elem.tag in simple_nodes:
        restrict_attributes(elem)
        return simple_nodes[elem.tag](children=get_child_nodes(elem))

    raise Exception(f"Unsupported tag {elem.tag}")

~~~

~~~ py
class DeleteNode(ContainerNode):
    def as_text(self) -> str:
        return f"~~{self.children_text()}~~"

    def as_html(self) -> SafeHtml:
        return self.tag("del")
~~~

And here is how I would have to serialize it according to the [docs](https://github.com/syntax-tree/mdast?tab=readme-ov-file#delete):

~~~ 
{
  type: 'delete',
  children: [{type: 'text', value: 'alpha'}]
}
~~~

**Steve Howell** · 2025-08-06 11:15 UTC

(replying to Tim Abbott)
> If you're interested in doing something in Python, I would suggest looking at whether a Pydantic implementation of their `mdast` is easy -- that would be an excellent way to evaluate whether we'll be happy with this ecosystem.

I didn't do this particular exercise, but I can say with 100% confidence that Pydantic would work with `mdast`, but that doesn't really buy us much, since the tricky bits are all related to the Zulip extensions.  The `mdast` paradigm is completely sane, but it's not exactly rocket science to come up with the idea of representing a tree of HTML-based nodes into JSON.

I think the more convincing findings I have had is that my Python [implementation](https://github.com/showell/zulip-flet/blob/main/api/content.py) was very easy to converge to the same basic shape as the Flutter/Content [representation of nodes](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/blob/main/lib/model/content.dart).  I don't dig as deep on Katex as the Flutter code, and there are some quibbles I'd have about granularity of nodes (I prefer super concrete classes such as ` UserGroupMentionSilentNode`), but the two modules are now quite similar apart from being written in different languages.

So I would think we'd basically want to leverage the decisions that we've already made in terms of Flutter (which is battle-tested by an app along with automated tests) and Python (which is battle-tested by round-trip validation against a decent corpus of messages).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-08-06 17:12 UTC

I think it's very reasonable to imagine, if we're building a set of tools that operate with a nice layer, something that converts third-party HTML into the Zulip AST format, as something broadly parallel to how we can convert Zulip HTML into the Zulip AST format. Just to lay out the places we'd use these classes of things we have today:
- Obviously sending an actual message starts with Markdown and produces HTML. Though maybe we could allow sending in other formats, there's going to need to be a data-population layer somewhere in the server's pipeline to resolve mentions and the like based on whether that user exists.
- The incoming email gateway will, for HTML-only emails, convert third-party HTML to Zulip Markdown today.
- The web app paste handler (`turndown`) converts HTML that may be Zulip or may be third-party into Zulip Markdown. This needs to be able to run in the web app for latency reasons, which means TypeScript or something that compiles to WebAssembly. (Presumably, mobile would want something similar).
- "Quote message" converts Zulip HTML into Markdown, at least when processing part of the message.
- A migration to clean the database of legacy HTML anomalies would want to take (at times 5+ years old or buggy) Zulip HTML and convert it into an AST and then into modern Zulip HTML that could be generated by the current Markdown processor, maybe with a check that the AST-to-Markdown conversion looks like the original Markdown. (We can't use the source Markdown alone, at least, since data about how say a mention was resolved at the time is not available today).
- Integrations (say, the Slack=>Zulip mirror) and data imports tools often need to convert third-party HTML into Zulip Markdown to generate Zulip messages. For most of these, we understand a lot about the third-party HTML and want to be able to process special elements like mentions.
- We'd want to think about what format(s) are best for storage in the database and/or sending to clients over the API. ASTs tend to be larger than the HTML, but I don't know the impact on things you actually care about (compressed size and parsing runtime).

<rant>
Last but not least, I think the reason to formalize a message AST for Zulip is that it will enable writing brand new Zulip clients.  Think about university students.  Think about folks that are integrating Zulip into another app (e.g. lean-programming proofs).  Think about folks that are just finicky about how the app works (e.g. yours truly).

Every single current Zulip app has limitations:
* zulip core -- too much legacy, too much jQuery in particular, too much surface area, too monolithic, too much dev setup,  too hard to hack
* desktop app -- barely maintained and a PITA
* mobile legacy -- obviously deprecated
* mobile Flutter - written in Dart
* zulip-terminal -- only works in the terminal

I'm mostly sympathetic to university students.  A reasonably competent sophomore CS student should be able to write a semi-usable Zulip client within a semester.  A talented college senior should be able to write a Zulip client within about three weeks that's at least better in some dimension than the main app.

I also think that everybody who writes the newest sexy JS framework should be able to produce a Zulip chat app for their canonical example, and it should render mentions.

## no retry mechanism in send_push_notification

*2025-07-22 to 2025-07-22 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/no.20retry.20mechanism.20in.20send_push_notification/with/2226881)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-07-22 12:45 UTC

In `send_apple_push_notification`, when APNs returns some error (apart from expired token), we simply log the error and return `apple_successfully_sent_count=0`. Is this intentional ? 

Ideally, there should be a retry mechanism ?

Similar thing happens in android code path.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-07-22 18:33 UTC

Part of the issue is that for the push bouncer, we're doing it synchronously while the client waits.  So we can't have too much backoff-and -retry.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-22 19:40 UTC

I think the server may retry, though?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-22 19:41 UTC

I think it is potentially correct to not retry from the bouncer and just have a single place where retries are done for a given request, but I'm not certain.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-07-22 19:45 UTC

The remote server does not retry unless it got an explicit "try again later" exception.  Which I don't think it does in this case -- and would possibly be wrong, in the case that, say, APNs went through but FCM didn't.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-22 20:06 UTC

Hmm, yeah, that's a good argument for potentially doing a retry in the bouncer for potentially transient APNs errors.


## JSON Web Key Set support

*2025-07-23 to 2026-01-09 · 10 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/JSON.20Web.20Key.20Set.20support/with/2227962)*

**MH35** · 2025-07-23 09:46 UTC

I want to use jwks.json, but the setting has no way.
`JWT_AUTH_KEYS` must have `key` and `algorithms` fields, but jwks.json may have more than one key.

I think it will be achieved by this fix in zerver/views/auth.py.
```python
def get_email_and_realm_from_jwt_authentication_request(
    request: HttpRequest, *, json_web_token: str
) -> tuple[str, Realm]:
    realm = get_realm_from_request(request)
    if realm is None:
        raise InvalidSubdomainError

    try:
        domain_auth_keys = settings.JWT_AUTH_KEYS[realm.subdomain]
    except KeyError:
        raise JsonableError(_("JWT authentication is not enabled for this organization"))

    # JWK verification
    if "jwks_url" in domain_auth_keys:
        try:
            jwks_client = jwt.PyJWKClient(domain_auth_keys["jwks_url"])
        except jwt.PyJWKClientConnectionError:
            raise JsonableError(_("Failed to fetch JSON Web Key Set"))
        except jwt.PyJWKClientError:
            raise JsonableError(_("JSON Web Key Set decode failed"))
        if not json_web_token:
            raise JsonableError(_("No JSON web token passed in request"))
        try:
            key = jwks_client.get_signing_key_from_jwt(json_web_token)
        except jwt.PyJWKClientError:
            raise JsonableError(_("Bad JSON web token"))
        algorithms = [key.algorithm_name]
    else:
        try:
            key = domain_auth_keys["key"]
            algorithms = domain_auth_keys["algorithms"]
        except KeyError:
            raise JsonableError(_("JWT authentication is not enabled for this organization"))
        if not json_web_token:
            raise JsonableError(_("No JSON web token passed in request"))

    try:
        options = {"verify_signature": True, "verify_aud": False}
        payload = jwt.decode(json_web_token, key, algorithms=algorithms, options=options)
    except jwt.InvalidTokenError:
        raise JsonableError(_("Bad JSON web token"))

    remote_email = payload.get("email", None)
    if remote_email is None:
        raise JsonableError(_("No email specified in JSON web token claims"))

    return remote_email, realm
```

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-07-23 18:41 UTC

As discussed in #**design>channel folders management UI**, we want to support changing the order in which channel folders are shown in left sidebar. I was thinking if we should use a DB structure similar to what we do for custom profile fields.

We can have a `order` field in `ChannelFolder` object which will be an integer field storing the position of the folder like we do for `CustomProfileField`.

I think the first step to making our current Python markdown implementation be a properly layered system is to just break up the 3000-line module using basic common sense. ## protected history channels optimizations

*2025-08-11 to 2025-08-29 · 6 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/protected.20history.20channels.20optimizations/with/2240990)*

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-08-11 18:25 UTC

One thing that's been a bit on my mind is whether we can significantly optimize Zulip for many users by keeping track of which users or realms have any channels with protected history; various algorithms can be more efficient in terms of how we do the SQL queries if we know that no channels of that type are in the messages a user can query, which should be true for the vast majority of queries.

Right now, we have some optimizations that take advantage of this to make access of (web-)public channels faster. But I wonder if we can materially reduce total load on the database related to fetching messages by doing something clever here.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-08-11 18:26 UTC

I expect it to be the case that 95%+ of total message fetching is from users who do not have access to any protected history channels.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-08-14 12:51 UTC

Can you define more precisely what it means for a stream to have protected history with respect to a certain user?  Is this mostly about private streams which I may have joined after initial conversations that I'm not allowed to see?

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-08-14 14:35 UTC

Just whether the user has any protected history channels that they have access to. Could consider just checking at the realm level for something easy to maintain; most realms won't have any.

**Steve Howell** · 2025-08-15 01:25 UTC

I like the idea of starting out realm granularity first.  Seems like a relatively easy win.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-08-29 22:01 UTC

I imagine we'd use abstractions that take a `UserProfile` object, and what that function does can change over time. But yes, realm level would be much easier to maintain, and might be a lot of the value.

(Or it might not -- like in chat.zulip.org, we have some protected history channels, but I bet 99% of users aren't in any).

**Pieter K** · 2025-08-27 14:48 UTC

#34275 wants to remove a guardrail for "Standard export" that prevents generating export with no usable owner/admin accounts. I just want to confirm, should this apply only to standard exports, or to public exports as well?

**Pieter K** · 2025-08-28 07:36 UTC

We currently have these two checks that prevents users from generating "dysfunctional" export data.

```python
def check_export_with_consent_is_usable(realm: Realm) -> bool:
    # Users without consent enabled will end up deactivated in the exported
    # data. An organization without a consenting Owner would therefore not be
    # functional after export->import. That's most likely not desired by the user
    # so check for such a case.
    consented_user_ids = get_consented_user_ids(realm)
    return UserProfile.objects.filter(
        id__in=consented_user_ids, role=UserProfile.ROLE_REALM_OWNER, realm=realm
    ).exists()


def check_public_export_is_usable(realm: Realm) -> bool:
    # Since users with email visibility set to NOBODY won't have their real emails
    # exported, this could result in a lack of functional Owner accounts.
    # We make sure that at least one Owner can have their real email address exported.
    return UserProfile.objects.filter(
        role=UserProfile.ROLE_REALM_OWNER,
        email_address_visibility__in=[
            UserProfile.EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_EVERYONE,
            UserProfile.EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_MEMBERS,
            UserProfile.EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_MODERATORS,
            UserProfile.EMAIL_ADDRESS_VISIBILITY_ADMINS,
        ],
        realm=realm,
    ).exists()
``` 
The definition of dysfunctional here seems to be: no accessible owner account.

Description in #34275:
> Remove the error when no owners have their email exported. Export should still run in this situation.

Do we want to update how we determine whether a realm is dysfunctional -- maybe to something like: make sure at least one admin (not owner) account is still accessible -- or do we want to scrap these guardrails completely?

## gc in GET /messages

*2025-09-11 to 2025-09-11 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/gc.20in.20GET.20.2Fmessages/with/2258343)*

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-09-11 14:20 UTC

When working on #35804, I saw some weird long-tail timings.  Since this profiling was via `zilencer/management/commands/profile_request.py`, calling the backend rendering function directly, nothing outside of Python (e.g. uwsgi, nginx, etc) was the cause; the slow runs also did not have more time in the database of memcached, either.

Comparing cprofile runs, generally the 300+ ms requests appeared to have 200ms pauses in random places -- e.g. in `extract_message_dict` but not the `orjson.loads` that is its single line within it.

Sticking a `gc.collect()` before each iteration of the loop (outside of the timing of the request) chopped off that long tail:

[get_messages access times, with hot caches.png](https://chat.zulip.org/user_uploads/2/b5/M_gkh9PMhckyecfy7wy0A7x1/get_messages-access-times-with-hot-caches-3.png)

[memray](https://github.com/bloomberg/memray) doesn't show any leaks.  I briefly experimented with [Scalene](https://github.com/plasma-umass/scalene) for the first time, but couldn't get much comprehensible out of it.

I don't expect there's any magic solution to this besides "don't use a GC'd language."  We don't appear to be doing anything obviously wrong, and I don't believe there's much we can do to avoid inflating the message objects from the cache when using them.

It may be interesting to see if the new [incremental GC in Python 3.14](https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#incremental-garbage-collection) changes things at all.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-09-11 14:24 UTC

Tangentially: @Anders Kaseorg, I noticed that a47c8ce15f5657dcf690ad4087047205606e2d3d added a `<3.14` limit -- why, out of curiosity?

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2025-09-11 19:52 UTC

It worked around a [dependency issue](https://github.com/hynek/argon2-cffi-bindings/blob/25.1.0/pyproject.toml#L6) that’s now been resolved upstream with the release of cffi 2.0.0 this Monday.

## active_mobile_push_notification

*2025-09-30 to 2025-10-14 · 37 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/active_mobile_push_notification/with/2268217)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-09-30 14:41 UTC

35cb7528f9def3631aa00d96e7b318c6cd229c6b commit message mentions:
> `active_mobile_push_notification` flag should never appear on a message that is also marked as read;

which is correct. But I think there's a possibility where user-messages can be marked as read with `active_mobile_push_notification` flag not cleared.

While marking messages as read we call `do_clear_mobile_push_notifications_for_ids` which enqueues events to `missedmessage_mobile_notifications` queue to "clear notifications on devices + unset `active_mobile_push_notification` flag".

`missedmessage_mobile_notifications` queue `"remove"` handler (`handle_remove_push_notification`) returns early if `push_notifications_configured` is False. So, we're left with user-messages marked as read but `active_mobile_push_notification` not cleared.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-09-30 14:41 UTC

Proposed solution:
* We should move the query which clears `active_mobile_push_notification` flag to `do_clear_mobile_push_notifications_for_ids` - i.e. we should clear the flag even before sending the event to `missedmessage_mobile_notifications` queue.
* Logically, it sounds a bit odd that we're clearing the flag even before actually trying to clear the notification on device. But in reality we make our best attempt to clear notification (it's not guaranteed) and clear the `active_mobile_push_notification` flag. So, I think it's fine to clear the flag early.
* We can simply clear the flag early in `handle_remove_push_notification` instead of moving it to `do_clear_mobile_push_notifications_for_id`, but it'd help to simplify things for #36121 if we take the second approach.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-09-30 14:41 UTC

Also, we need a migration to fix such rows.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-09-30 14:45 UTC

Let me know if this sounds fine or if there're any other views.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-09-30 20:46 UTC

So the core question here is how things should work when there's queueing delay or events in the queue are lost. 
- If events in the queue are lost, then in practice, that "remove" mobile notification will never be sent. In which case we are better off having `active_mobile_push_notification` having already been cleared by the process marking the message as read. But a defensible alternative would be a separate mechanism, like a cron job, that scan for messages in with `read && active_mobile_push_notification` and sends the delayed "remove" push notifications for them.
- If the events are delayed, then having cleared `active_mobile_push_notification` early changes what metrics are available for us to understand the scope of the problem; though the queue size would be a usable metric.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-09-30 21:19 UTC

I'm not sure what the best path forward is here, would appreciate others' thoughts.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2025-10-06 05:36 UTC

I think the cron job mechanism is the best among those options.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-06 19:17 UTC

@Alex Vandiver thoughts on this architecture question?

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-10-06 19:29 UTC

I'm really not convinced that a cron job to handle the edge case of "we lost data in our queues" is defensible.  As long as the state isn't inconsistent, it's fine if data loss leads to the system ending up in a different consistent state.

Like, we're not going to advocate for adding a table to track the emails we're going to send, just so that if the `email_senders` queue events are lost, that we can repopulate that queue.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-06 19:35 UTC

Yeah, I think I agree. Especially given our design direction of potentially moving some queues to postgres, where transactions can protect them from being lost independently from the database, I think we don't want that cron job in the picture.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-06 19:36 UTC

But I guess I'm feeling like I may be missing something. We were definitely very intentional about clearing the flag atomically at the time that the remove notification actually gets sent, and while it's possible we weren't thinking it through clearly, I wonder if I'm missing something.

I think after refreshing my memory a bit, the most likely story is just that we conceived of the `active_mobile_push_notification` flag as meaning exactly what it says on the tin: Something that should not be cleared until we've actually completed the action to notify the user's clients that the notification is no longer active.

And that the main downside of clearing that when we flip the `read` flag would be that flag's name requiring slightly more definition, and a change in the exact process of debugging any weird situations where a remove mobile notification doesn't arrive.

I think, we can read `active_mobile_push_notification` as `sent_and_unrevoked_mobile_push_notification`. Currently, we define it as:

* We set `active_mobile_push_notification = False` after the server attempted to revoke the notif. Marking it `False` early on (which was the earlier proposal) makes this definition written in comment wrong.

In general a commit message from the past is never authoritative about the present — they're a record of what change was intended at the time and why, and by nature they can't be updated later. So it's normal for the way things work now to disagree with something we wrote in an old commit message.

The place we should try to keep in sync with our current thinking is any comments in the current tree.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-14 23:16 UTC

Yeah I agree with all that.

## inline-image corner cases

*2025-10-15 to 2025-12-30 · 26 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/inline-image.20corner.20cases/with/2278041)*

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-15 17:02 UTC

With #36226 getting nearer to being ready for test deployment on CZO, I wanted to point out a few corner cases with the `![]()` syntax that need to be addressed still:

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-15 17:05 UTC

The first case is **external images presented in the Markdown image syntax**. These are currently only partially processed by the `ImageInlineProcessor` class in `zerver/lib/markdown/__init__.py`, which is to say that external images get a `data-original-src` attribute, but nothing else. That leaves external images in bare `<img>` tags that allow the image to occupy the full width of the message area--making them potentially massively larger than their uploaded counterparts.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-15 17:10 UTC

The second case is **non-image files presented in Markdown image syntax**.

Currently, **uploaded non-image files** simply render the message with the original markdown string, with or without custom alt text.

By contrast, references to **external non-image files** exhibit one of two behaviors:

1. When alt text is presented (`![example alt text](https://example.com/example.pdf)`), the alt text is rendered on the image--which is expected browser behavior in the face of a broken image. But there is still of course an `<img src="https://example.com/example.pdf" alt="example alt text" />` presented in the rendered message.
2. Worse, when alt text is *not* presented (`![][(https://example.com/example.pdf)`), nothing is rendered, but the image tag is again presented in the rendered message: `<img src="https://example.com/example.pdf" />`. When such Markdown is the only message content, this effectively renders a blank message.

**Alex Vandiver** · 2025-10-15 17:14 UTC

How does, e.g., Github handle those two cases?

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-15 17:18 UTC

That's a good question. Let me check and report back.

The other thing to note with the first case is that external images linked to from the legacy syntax (e.g., `[](https://stolley.dev/assets/img/ksrtc-800w.jpg)`) are delivered from the server as an otherwise unadorned `<img>` element with just a `src` attribute and tucked inside the expected `<a>`element. In post-processing, we add both a `media-image-element` class (which CSS leverages to keep the size of these things in check) and the `loading="lazy"` attribute.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-15 17:24 UTC

What I'm imagining to address both of those issues is the following:
- We'll know whether the linked item is an uploaded image or other media element via our thumbnailing pipeline.
- If the link is to anything that is not an uploaded media element, we generate identical HTML to the link syntax (i.e. as though the `!` is not there).

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-15 17:25 UTC

I believe if we do that, then neither of these potentially problematic corner cases will be possible.

**Karl Stolley** · 2025-10-15 17:26 UTC

(replying to Alex Vandiver)
> How does, e.g., Github handle those two cases?

You can see [the results on GitHub](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/36226#issuecomment-3407515658). GitHub does kind of what we're doing now--no alt text, no visible indication that something is there (or that something is amiss). When there is alt text, it's linked--like our legacy images--to the original source. That happens with both uploaded non-image files and their external counterparts.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-15 17:26 UTC

If in the future, we extend our thumbnailing pipeline to support additional media elements (non-uploaded, or other file formats), we would just move those from the set that get converted into a link to the set that generate a media preview.

**Tim Abbott** · 2025-10-15 17:28 UTC

I've not looked into how the Markdown processor logic would work. But if we were using a vanilla CommonMark base processor, this will surely look like a post-processor that turns Markdown `<img>` elements into a link or a Zulip image element with all our thumbnailing metadata, depending on the URL.
