3. Api key rotation/device key rotation.
  The device record carries `push_key` (server-side only, never exposed via API) and `push_key_id` (exposed on the device object). Unlike `push_account_id`, `push_key_id` isn't a stable identifier for the account — it's expected to change every time the client rotates its key, since the client mints a new `push_key_id` alongside each new `push_key`. It's included in notification payloads instead of `push_account_id`.
  This directly solves the client's key-rotation state-tracking problem (from the second linked message): the client just looks at whatever `push_key_id` currently sits on its device object — old or new — to know which generation of key is currently active server-side, without needing a separate side-channel to track "did my rotation take effect yet."

**Aditya** · 2026-07-09 04:36 UTC

Hey @Emily Sutherlin  thanks for posting it here, I was the one who raised the PR but got busy later so couldn't proceed further, will try to look into it again as per Tim's advise.

**Aditya** · 2026-07-10 09:19 UTC

hello, so after putting some thought into it and taking inspiration from the approach Tim suggested, I replaced the `UnnestLinks` approach with a different design.

instead  of generating nested links and cleaning them up afterwards, I introduced a `SemiAtomicString` variant of `AtomicString`. It allows standard Markdown processors (like emphasis) to operate normally inside link text, while Zulip's custom link-generating processors recognize it and explicitly skip creating links (`is_link_pattern=True`), preventing nested `<a>` tags from being generated in the first place.

to make this work, I adjusted the processor priorities so the standard `LinkInlineProcessor` runs before Zulip's custom linkifiers. This means Markdown links are parsed first, their inner text is wrapped in `SemiAtomicString`, and the custom linkifiers naturally ignore that content.

this feels closer to the direction Tim suggested as it avoids that extra cleanup pass and and addresses the issue during parsing instead of after the fact. I'd appreciate any thoughts on whether this seems like a more robust approach or if there are edge cases I should still be considering.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 20:52 UTC

Yeah this sounds plausibly reasonable. Though I would confirm that CommonMark processors handle this correctly, and note that attention spent on this could be being spent on migrating to a modern CommonMark-based base processor.

## Races on SAML login

*2026-07-14 to 2026-07-16 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Races.20on.20SAML.20login/with/2495246)*

**Gary** · 2026-07-14 23:39 UTC

I was digging into [#36871](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/36871) last week, it ended up being somewhat more complicated than I'd initially expected. :slight_smile: I wrote up [a more detailed report on the issue](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/issues/36871#issuecomment-4964329928), but the summary of the problem is:

- There are two races here. One for adding user group rows, and one for removing them. If the former occurs, an error will be thrown. If the latter occurs, there won't be an error, but there will be duplicated log entries and corresponding `remove_members` events.
- There are related systems that can trigger additional races or deadlocks: LDAP cron can lead to many row locks, creating groups when two different users is race-y, and potential deadlocks with subgroups.

One approach I considered for solving the initial problem was to get a lock on the `UserProfile` row, so simultaneous logins would be serialised, and they can each recalculate their changed user groups once they gain the lock. This doesn't address the related issues, but would solve the initial issue.

An alternative I considered was look into making this functionality more fault tolerant. For example, allowing query conflicts to fail safely, then generating logs and events based on what actually changed in the DB.

I'd really appreciate additional input on all of this: whether I've missed anything in my report, what's generally considered to be the more reliable approach in Zulip, and potentially if there's room to look at replacing the locking approach with a fault tolerant approach. As a general rule, I find that locking works great when all cases can be accounted for, but is more likely to have edge cases; whereas fault tolerance is more flexible, but when it does have edge cases, they're usually weirder, and harder to diagnose. :upside_down:

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-07-15 16:01 UTC

@Gary Thanks for the thoughtful investigation! 

I think this approach from your comment on the issue is the most solid?

> Because this race is per-user, one idea I considered was to serialise concurrent syncs of the same user with `select_for_update(no_key=True)` on the `UserProfile` row (the same behaviour as `do_change_user_role`, for example). Once we've gained the `UserProfile` row lock, we can then lock only the `NamedUserGroup` rows in the computed diff, re-read the user's memberships in just those groups, and drop already-satisfied operations.

Though I'm not sure if the `UserProfile` lock contributes anything really helpful here; or if we should do only the group-locking part?

Group creation races from ``ensure_missing_groups`` can probably just be handled with `ON CONFLICT` handling as suggested, or just a simple `try/except IntegrityError` approach to catch the exception.

**Gary** · 2026-07-16 04:51 UTC

The `UserProfile` lock was definitely the most solid idea I settled on, but it was the edge cases that gave me pause. The LDAP cron transaction looks like it could lock up a lot of rows until it finishes, but I'm not entirely sure how likely that is to occur in practical scenarios.

We need the `UserProfile` lock (as opposed to locking just the `NamedUserGroup` rows) to address the issue of a user racing against themselves in two separate login processes: it forces them to act sequentially, and gives us a safe section in which to compute the group changes, then apply them. Once the first process commits, the second one will gain the lock, compute the (now empty) set of group changes, then continue.

Because complicated locking dependencies is often a great way to end up with weird hard-to-reproduce deadlock issues, I thought it was worth at least considering take a more fault tolerant approach, but that's a more substantial architectural decision.

## compression bug in event queue

*2026-07-19 to 2026-07-23 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/compression.20bug.20in.20event.20queue/with/2497444)*

**Ahmed Tabish** · 2026-07-19 05:37 UTC

in `zerver/tornado/event_queue.py` i found a `#BUG` on the event-queue compression logic in `EventQueue.push()`

i tried to reproduce a concrete case in manage.py shell (no db needed, purely in memory)

read(101) -> unread(101) -> read(202)

Expected: 101 ends up "unread" because thats the last thing that happened to it

Actual: 
`1 remove read [101]
2 add read [101, 202]`

101 ends up read.

**The issue:** to avoid flooding queues with many small events, `push()` merges consecutive `flags/add/read` events into a single "virtual event" (eg: many messages marked read in a row become one combined event). `flags/remove/read` (mark-unread) events are deliberately *not* merged. 
The problem: a merged virtual event's position in the queue is updated to wherever its *most recent* merge happened, not preserved from its first occurrence. So an unrelated "read" event on a *different* message can push the merged event's position past an intervening "unread" event on the *original* message, reordering them for the client.

A client applying these in order marks 101 unread, then read, ending in the wrong final state. So a user can mark a message unread and have it silently flip back to read on another open client, just because of unrelated read activity on a different message batched in afterward.

Wanted to raise this for discussion before proposing a fix, since it touches the core event-delivery path and I want to make sure I'm not missing context on why the compression is structured this way before changing it.

**Anders Kaseorg** · 2026-07-27 20:01 UTC

I think it’s time to go ahead with switching from the system `/usr/bin/python` to the Python binary [managed by `uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/python-versions/#managed-python-distributions): #37835.

This will immediately bump our baseline Python version from 3.10 to 3.14, letting us take advantage of new Python features and optimizations, giving us the option to extend the support lifetime on older OS releases, and unblocking important upstream upgrades that have already dropped older Python support such as Django 6.0. And it will let us accelerate our adoption schedule for future Python versions, which is becoming increasingly necessary as upstream dependencies also trend toward this acceleration.

Probably the first step is testing on chat.zulip.org, though the main parts that aren’t fully tested in situ involve the assorted scripts that run for database-only hosts and Nagios and stuff, so we’ll need to watch carefully when deploying on Cloud.

## inconsistency in WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED audit logs

*2026-08-04 to 2026-09-04 · 5 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/inconsistency.20in.20WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED.20audit.20logs/with/2504758)*

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-08-04 15:46 UTC

There is a slight inconsistency in when we create `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` audit log entries when changing role. 

Quoting from [here](https://github.com/zulip/zulip/pull/39873#discussion_r3705238556)-
> When changing role, we add and remove user from system groups by directly using `UserGroupMembership.objects` queries and not use helpers like `bulk_add_members_to_user_groups`. But to add or remove users from full members group we use `update_users_in_full_members_system_group` which uses `bulk_add_members_to_user_groups` and thus a `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` entry is created if the `workplace_users_group` is set to `full members` group.
> 
> Like when changing a role from guest to moderator and `workplace_users_group` set to `full members`, three audit log entries are created - with event types `USER_ROLE_CHANGED`, `USER_GROUP_DIRECT_USER_MEMBERSHIP_ADDED` and `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED`. But when changing role from member to moderator and `workplace_users_group` set to `moderators`, only `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` and `USER_GROUP_DIRECT_USER_MEMBERSHIP_ADDED` entries are created even when workplace users count changes.
> 
> This isn't correctness problem since we would eventually get the correct count either through `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` or `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` after the fix in the PR.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 19:50 UTC

I recommend documenting this in a comment somewhere near code that needs to understand it, if it's something we can't clean up.

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-08-19 13:24 UTC

There are a couple of ways to make it consistent, i.e. audit logs should not depend on what type of role change was done.
- One way can be that we can skip creating `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` audit log entry for role change and rely on count data in `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` entry.
- One can be to just create the `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` entry for each addition or removal from a group if that group is used as workplace users group, either directly or indirectly as a subgroup.
- One other way can be to create exactly one `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` entry if at least one of the old role system group, new role system group or full members system group (if user is added or removed from full members group) is used as workplace users group either directly or indirectly as a subgroup.

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-09-03 17:32 UTC

I merged #39873, so we should make sure not to lose track of this before deciding what to do.

I'm not that deep in this code to cast a confident vote, but:
> One way can be that we can skip creating `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` audit log entry for role change and rely on count data in `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` entry.

Sounds like a reasonable simplification?  Since `WORKPLACE_USERS_COUNT_CHANGED` seems to just duplicate info from `USER_ROLE_CHANGED` in this case?

**Sahil Batra** · 2026-09-04 11:58 UTC

Yes. Opened #40084 for this.


## ✔ n+1 queries in custom profile field update endpoint

*2026-08-06 to 2026-09-28 · 7 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/.E2.9C.94.20n.2B1.20queries.20in.20custom.20profile.20field.20update.20endpoint/with/2505937)*

**Ahmed Tabish** · 2026-08-06 11:47 UTC

I found that updating "n" custom profile fields in a single request costs roughly 3-4 DB queries per field

* `validate_user_custom_profile_data` (`zerver/lib/users.py`) does one `CustomProfileField.objects.get()` per field in the request.
* `do_update_user_custom_profile_data_if_changed` (`zerver/actions/custom_profile_fields.py`) does one `get_or_create()` per field, plus a separate lazy `.field` FK fetch per field (no `select_related`) for the `is_renderable()` check.

Measured this end-to-end via `assert_database_query_count` on a realm with 9 custom fields:



**44 queries** for "one save profile click" touching all 9 fields, this will scale linearly with the number of fields in the request, and there's no cap on how many custom fields a realm can define,

so larger orgs will pay proportionally more.


I've added a query-count regression test to lock in this baseline, that batches these into bulk fetches (`filter(id__in=...)` + `bulk_update`/`bulk_create`), to bring this down to a small constant number of queries regardless of n. Wanted to flag the approach here before finishing the patch in case there's context I'm missing

Would love to get another pair of eyes on this

## use threading to download files instead of multiprocessing.

*2026-08-07 to 2026-08-09 · 3 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/use.20threading.20to.20download.20files.20instead.20of.20multiprocessing.2E/with/2506433)*

**Pieter K** · 2026-08-07 12:14 UTC

Currently, we use `run_parallel_queue` to do multiprocessing for tasks that spend most of their time waiting for network requests and/or file operations (mostly in third-party import tools). Should we instead use threading for those cases? The cost for each worker is cheaper, and we could potentially use more of them. Pooling results (like attachment records) and interacting with global variables (like `NEXT_ID`) from each worker should also be simpler.

I used `time.perf_counter` to profile the Slack importer's `download_and_export_upload_file`, and I think we'd benefit from threading there:
```
PROFILE 45842   request=0.6854  mkdir=0.0008    write=0.0004    total=0.6866
```

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-08-07 16:51 UTC

I think the main, high-level answer is that we actually generally **want** the  isolation we get from running tasks in separate processes, to avoid the tangly bugs that you easily run into when they share address space when using threads. More difficulty with the occasional required cooperation (like pooling results) between the tasks is not a big cost to pay for that.

**Tim Abbott** · 2026-08-09 16:01 UTC

There is probably some benefit to reducing memory overflow risk. But I think it's likely not very important overall, and especially performance-wise.

## Allow self-hosted orgs to be listed in communities directory

*2026-08-24 to 2026-09-28 · 20 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Allow.20self-hosted.20orgs.20to.20be.20listed.20in.20communities.20directory/with/2514206)*

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:34 UTC

We're planning to add support to **Allow self-hosted organizations to be listed in communities directory** - #23419

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:34 UTC

Currently it is supported only for Zulip Cloud orgs. See: https://zulip.com/help/communities-directory

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:35 UTC

Posting a high level design of how I think it should work, any suggestions/feedback would be helpful.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:35 UTC

Self hosted servers and the zulip bouncer are the two components involved.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:35 UTC

### On server

* Add `ZULIP_SERVICE_ADVERTISE_REALM` - a new Zulip service.
* Server admin needs to set `ZULIP_SERVICE_ADVERTISE_REALM = True` and run `./manage.py register_server`
* The minimum amount of data server needs to send to the bouncer for this service to work will be `AnalyticsDataUploadLevel.BASIC`.
   * We mainly need the value of `realm.want_advertise_in_communities_directory` and `realm.url`. 
   * The `want_advertise_in_communities_directory` field is currently not included in `BASIC` level, so we'll include that.
   * We can introduce a new `AnalyticsDataUploadLevel` for this service as well.. if we want to keep `BASIC` reserved for `security_alerts` service.
* Realm admins can toggle the realm setting `want_advertise_in_communities_directory` to get their realm advertised.
* Analytics cron job running on server keeps the fields of our importance updated on bouncer.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 12:36 UTC

### On bouncer

* Add two boolean fields on `RemoteRealm` - `want_advertise_in_communities_directory` and `advertise_in_communities_directory_approved`. **Let's call it `want_advertise` and `advertise_approved` for this discussion.**
* A new cron job runs on bouncer which, for each `RemoteRealm` with `want_advertise = True`:
   * Makes a call to [`GET /server_settings`](https://zulip.com/api/get-server-settings), uses it's response to check [eligibility](https://zulip.com/help/communities-directory#eligibility) for getting advertised.
   * If eligibility met, set `advertise_approved = True` for the remote realm. Also store `realm_description` and `realm_icon` on the remote realm table, returned in the response - it is needed for the /communities page. 
   * If eligibility not met, set `advertise_approved = False` (if it was set to True due to meeting eligibility earlier)
 * In `communities_view`, fetch remote realms with `want_advertise = True` and `approve_advertise = True` - these are the remote realms which will be advertised.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-08-24 13:35 UTC

This sounds correct to me in the abstract. Will updates to the description, logo/icon, etc. be picked up by the cron job? Does that trigger a new approval process?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-08-24 14:15 UTC

Sounds pretty reasonable to me. So is the idea for eligibility to be determined completely automatically, via pinging the server, without a manual review/approval process?

**Mateusz Mandera** · 2026-08-24 14:18 UTC

Also, depending on the amount of servers that sign up for this, we might need to be careful about the frequency with which we do these re-checks to `GET /server_settings`, since these are outgoing requests to servers we don't control - some of them might be slow to respond, etc.

E.g. trying to ping `GET /server_settings` of 10,000 servers every day in a single cronjob would not be a great idea. (Not that we expect 10k signups for this - just an example).

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-08-24 14:48 UTC

Seems like we should have some kind of approval process for this, for spam/NSFW reasons if nothing else.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 14:49 UTC

Here's some prev discussion around orgs eligibility.

@Alya Abbott [said](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/101-design/topic/communities.20directory.20.2315844/near/1360818) in #**design>communities directory #15844**:
> The issue suggests restricting this feature to the `STANDARD_FREE` plan, but I don't think we should do that. I think we should see if the list actually ends up being "spammy", and potentially remove orgs from the list that's actually shown as a post-processing step (e.g. requiring activity in the l …

So, if the eligible orgs count increases to the extent of making that list spammy, the plan was to restricting the eligibility.

We already say on the help page: "To prevent spam, Zulip reserves the right to use editorial discretion. Giving Zulip permission to promote your organization in the communities directory does not guarantee that it will be listed."

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-08-24 14:50 UTC

(And while more of a frontend concern, we should probably add `rel="nofollow"` to the links in the communities directory.)

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 14:55 UTC

So, I think that addresses the "trying to ping `GET /server_settings` of 10,000 servers every day in a single cronjob would not be a great idea." concern.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 14:55 UTC

Regarding "a manual review/approval process".

Yeah, we can do this. Currently there's no manual review process for cloud orgs as well. So, it'll be a nice addition overall but with an added manual review work for the team.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 14:56 UTC

(replying to Karl Stolley)
> Will updates to the description, logo/icon, etc. be picked up by the cron job? Does that trigger a new approval process?

Yeah. Just no spam / NSFW check.

**Karl Stolley** · 2026-08-24 14:59 UTC

(replying to Prakhar Pratyush)
> Regarding "a manual review/approval process". Yeah, we can do this. Currently there's no manual review process for cloud orgs as well. So, it'll be a nice addition overall but with an added manual review work for the team.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-08-24 15:00 UTC

Yeah, that sounds better.

**Prakhar Pratyush** · 2026-09-22 06:27 UTC

## Idempotency - caching errors

*2026-09-04 to 2026-09-08 · 11 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Idempotency.20-.20caching.20errors/with/2519602)*

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-04 10:55 UTC

#36213 currently caches succeeded and failed responses in "an attempt" to avoid redoing any work (i.e., validation checks or actual successful work like new message)

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-04 11:03 UTC

Wait for upcoming messages to bring the rest of the context....

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-04 11:23 UTC

Here is my earlier concern opposing caching error:

1. I don't understand how it's beneficial. Wtih current changes, if a bad request is retired (with or without an Idempotency-key) the server just does the checking and returns the response indicating it's a bad request, what the benfit of caching it?
2. The current design scoop is the actual work itself (not the whole endpoint ) as it wraps the work with `idempotent_work`. I looked at two examples where idempotency is relevant: `update_message_backend` and `send_message_backend`, both of which chek and validate the request (potentially raising `JsonableError`) before the actual work itself, i.e. before `do_update_message` and `do_send_message` respectively.

So long story short, I don't see how caching error response is relevant here, at least with the current design.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-04 11:23 UTC

And here is @Tim Abbott reply on that concern

@Tim Abbott [said](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/Idempotency-Key.20HTTP.20header/near/2232785) in #**backend>Idempotency-Key HTTP header**:
> I believe the reason to store the error result is that if we receive a replayed request, the goal of this feature is to not repeat processing of that request a second time, whether it succeeded or failed.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-04 11:35 UTC

**I need to point out the tradeoffs here which I believe are what should decide which direction we should go:**

### Pros
It caches successful and failed requests, it's really generic and can be used with other non-idempotent endpoints. It clearly documents and tests every case; every case here means where exactly in the code path does the request fail or succeed. All cases are dcoumented and tested in `test_idempotent_request.py`

### Cons
The message sending code path (which is the only path using this idempotency system) does all validation checks **BEFORE** attempting the non-idempotent work (i.e., before `idempotent_work`). This is the most common failure for the message sending path (tested in `test_early_failure` test case). This simply means that caching error reponses in this partiuclar "common" case in useless because the server returns the failed response via the validation check code NOT the failed response the idempotency system cached

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-09-05 03:40 UTC

Great, thanks for laying it out. Since by removing the caching of errors, we are not breaking the feature, I think we should go ahead and remove it. It is very easy to add it back later.

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-06 19:30 UTC

#36213 is now updated; we now only cache successful requests

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-06 19:31 UTC

The documentation in the last commit is NOT updated yet, this shouldn't be a blocker for review though. Will try to update in the next few days

**Bedo Khaled** · 2026-09-06 19:33 UTC

**Please note that I updated but kept all existing test cases, they may seem redundant at first glance, but they are not**. All of these cases are potential scnearios (from rare to very common),  each one tests and documents the current behavior of not cahcing the response error.

## splitting long compositions #38357

*2026-10-12 to 2026-10-14 · 2 messages · [open in Zulip](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/3-backend/topic/splitting.20long.20compositions.20.2338357/with/2536848)*

**Sairam Bisoyi** · 2026-10-12 09:09 UTC

For PR #38357 @Sahil Batra  suggested in [#api design](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/channel/378-api-design/topic/split.20long.20messages.20PR.20.2338357/with/2510502) storing a scheduled split message as one row instead of N rows.

The original approach used multiple ScheduledMessage rows linked by split_group_id which could cause parts to return out of order, allow individual parts to be edited or deleted, and result in partial delivery. The new approach stores the full text in one row with the split_message_on_send boolean and splits it at delivery time.

The server-side zerver/lib/split_message.py mirrors the web app's splitting rule two consecutive blank lines outside code blocks with shared test cases ensuring consistency, including support for indented code. Each part is validated separately, with a maximum of 20 parts; oversized parts are rejected rather than truncated, and splitting stops early when the limit is exceeded.

Before delivery, every part is validated, then all are sent in one do_send_messages call, so delivery is all or nothing, with delivered_message_id storing the first part's ID. PATCH edits the whole message and can turn splitting on or off; turning it off only works if the text fits within a single message.

Does this look good?

**Aman (amanagr)** · 2026-10-14 07:22 UTC

I can look into after the 13.0 release.
